mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% signals sustained monetary accommodation that lowers discount rates for equity cash flows, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of periods with FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.5% in a 3-month window indicates labor market deterioration that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signal collapsing consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue expectations, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of periods with both HOUST and RSAFS declining, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production below 100 indicates supply chain contraction that increases input costs and compresses corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of INDPRO < 100 periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth above 2.0% signals robust economic expansion that boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >60% of GDPC1 growth >2.0% periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Year-over-year CPI inflation exceeding 3.5% triggers monetary tightening expectations that increase real interest rates and depress equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of CPIAUCSL > 3.5% YoY instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) signal labor market contraction that reduces household income and consumer spending, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of periods with PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise, or interaction term Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate above 4.0% indicates active monetary tightening that reduces liquidity and increases borrowing costs, depressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of FEDFUNDS > 4.0% periods, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year window.
